title: Capacitor Mindmap
notes: Comprehensive study of capacitance, parallel plate geometry, combinations, electrostatic energy, and dielectric polarization.
Covers core NEB formulas: C = Q/V, C = ε₀A/d, series/parallel networks, energy U = ½CV², and polarization P = χ_e ε₀ E.
Essential foundation for electrostatics, AC circuits, and semiconductor electronics.

subtopics.name: Definition & Units
points: C = Q / V (Ratio of charge to potential rise)
SI Unit: Farad (F) = 1 C/V, Dimensions: [M⁻¹ L⁻² T⁴ I²]
Isolated Sphere: C = 4πε₀R (Earth C ≈ 711 μF)

subtopics.name: Principle of Capacitor
points: Grounded secondary plate reduces potential of primary plate
Enables massive charge storage at low operating voltage

subtopics.name: Air / Vacuum Medium
points: Uniform field: E = σ/ε₀ = Q / (ε₀A)
Capacitance: C₀ = ε₀A / d

subtopics.name: Dielectric Slab Insertion
points: Partially filled slab (t < d): C = ε₀A / [d - t(1 - 1/κ)]
Conducting slab (t < d): C = ε₀A / (d - t)
Fully filled: C = κε₀A / d = κC₀

subtopics.name: Electrostatic Plate Attraction
points: Attractive force: F = Q² / (2ε₀A) = ½ ε₀ A (V/d)²
Factor of ½ arises because charge interacts only with the field of the opposite plate

subtopics.name: Series Combination
points: Identical charge Q on each capacitor
Reciprocal addition: 1/C_s = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ...
Two capacitors: C_s = (C₁C₂) / (C₁ + C₂)
Voltage divider: V₁ = [C₂/(C₁+C₂)]V

subtopics.name: Parallel Combination
points: Identical potential difference V across each branch
Direct addition: C_p = C₁ + C₂ + ...
Charge sharing: Q₁ = C₁V, Q₂ = C₂V

subtopics.name: Charge Redistribution & Energy Loss
points: Common potential: V_c = (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂) / (C₁ + C₂)
Energy loss: ΔU = ½ [C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂)](V₁ - V₂)²
Dissipated as heat and EM radiation

subtopics.name: Stored Electrostatic Energy
points: U = ½ CV² = Q² / (2C) = ½ QV
Work done by battery: W = QV = CV²
Charging efficiency: 50% stored, 50% lost as heat

subtopics.name: Energy Density in Medium
points: Energy per volume: u = ½ ε₀ E² (vacuum) or ½ ε E² (dielectric)
Energy is stored in the electric field itself

subtopics.name: Polar vs Non-Polar Dielectrics
points: Non-polar: Symmetric molecules (H₂, O₂, CO₂), zero permanent dipole
Polar: Asymmetric molecules (H₂O, HCl), permanent electric dipole

subtopics.name: Vectors E, P, and D
points: Reduced field: E = E₀ - E_p = E₀ / κ
Polarization vector: P = χ_e ε₀ E = σ_p (bound surface charge density)
Electric displacement: D = ε₀E + P = κε₀E = σ_free
Constitutive relation: κ = 1 + χ_e
